title: fix(pm): governed-merges self-test refuses as NOT MEASURED when its generator toolchain is absent
body:
Fixes #15272

In a freshly created worktree, before `pnpm install`, `pnpm check:pm-governed-merges` exited **1** — a finding's code — and reported:

```
self-test battery "#11705 end to end, against the REAL generator" registered 5 case(s),
below its pinned floor of 7 — cases that used to run no longer do.
A battery at or below its floor means cases STOPPED RUNNING — the battery is the bug, not
the number. Find what stopped registering (an early return, a deleted block, a guard that
now skips) and restore it.
```

Nothing had stopped running. Three sibling gates met the same worktree in the same minute and answered correctly with exit 3 `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`. This one reported a NOT MEASURED condition as a measured red, on a governance gate, and prescribed a hunt for code nobody deleted.

## The mechanism, measured

The card deliberately did not measure which dependency that battery loads. It is the generator toolchain, and the chain is:

1. The live case calls `runSinkGenerator`, which spawns `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec tsx scripts/build-skill-references.ts --check`.
2. In an uninstalled checkout that exits **254** with `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_EXEC_FIRST_FAIL  Command "tsx" not found` (measured directly, both through the function and through pnpm).
3. `runSinkGenerator` maps every failure — absent toolchain, spawn error, unreadable manifest, real drift — to the same `outputs: null` shape with a reason string. That is correct and deliberate for the AUDIT, where fail-closed is the ruled answer.
4. The self-test's live battery branches on that shape, taking its one-assertion path instead of its three-assertion path: 5 registered against a pinned 7.
5. The floor, which is doing exactly its job, renders that as cases that stopped running.

So the registration is silent rather than throwing because `spawnSync` returns a status and the code turns it into a reason — there is no exception anywhere on the path.

## The repair

- **`generatorToolchainPrerequisite(root, entry)`** asks whether the row's recompute can run at all, by looking for the same binary `pnpm exec` would resolve. Two remedies kept apart: nothing installed at all, and an install that does not carry the runner.
- It is consulted at the **top of `selfTest()`**, before a single case runs — not beside the battery — so the shared frame's load-bearing clause ("this gate exited before running a single check") is literally true when it prints.
- It is strictly a **narrowing of one exit code into another**. A checkout whose toolchain resolves takes the identical path it took before; a checkout whose toolchain does not exits 3 instead of 1. No branch in it can turn a red into a green, it cannot lift a governed path or lower a floor, and the audit paths (`--test`, the sweep) never consult it.
- ⛔ The reason string is deliberately **not** classified: an uninstalled checkout and a generator reporting genuine drift both arrive as a non-zero `--check` exit, so reading that text would fold a real finding into a refusal — the expensive direction.

### Reuse, not a sixth spelling

The exit-3 path is a **shared helper**: `scripts/import-prerequisite.mjs` exports `EXIT_PREREQUISITE_NOT_MET`, `INSTALL_FIX` and `reportPrerequisiteNotMet`, and every sibling that answers this class routes through it. This gate now does too — the code, the frame, the "Nothing was measured … It is NOT a finding" clause and the pipe advisory are all the repo's. The helper is **not edited**.

One thing it cannot express, reported rather than worked around: its advisory names the importer by **path**, which is right for the single-mode gates it was written for. This file has modes, and `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` without `--self-test` runs the network **sweep**. The helper takes no invocation argument, so the correct entry point (`pnpm check:pm-governed-merges`) is stated in this gate's own detail lines, where the claim about what went unmeasured already lives.

## Both directions pinned

`batteryFloorFailures()` is lifted to module scope and takes its ledger as an argument. It had no pin of its own — until it took its inputs there was no way to hand it a ledger — so the direction that matters most was asserted nowhere. Its behaviour, its order and every message it prints are unchanged; ledger fixtures are built **from** this roster, so each message quotes the real pinned number.

New battery, 17 cases (245 → 262 assertions):

- an uninstalled checkout is a prerequisite miss naming `node_modules`, and prescribes the install
- an install lacking the runner names the **runner**, not a missing tree
- the checkout this run loaded from meets it, so every floor below judges exactly as before
- the refusal code is the repo-wide 3, never a finding's 1
- **end to end**, on a copy of this file's own module graph in a checkout with no `node_modules`: exit 3, naming the class, the prerequisite and the remedy, stating in words that nothing was measured, and no longer printing the shrunken-battery diagnosis
- a ledger one case short still reds and still names **that** battery; one that never ran is named `DID NOT RUN`; an assertion under no declared battery and a shrunk roster are both named; a full ledger produces nothing

## A defect the ablation found, and closed

Ablating the probe turned the end-to-end fixture into an **unbounded chain of self-tests** — the child reaches that battery only when the probe did not refuse, and there its own copied tree is a perfect seed for the next copy. Measured: one process per second, 67 of them before it was cut off by hand. A hang is the worst reading a gate can return, neither green nor red and indistinguishable from slow. The child is now marked in its argv, a marked run refuses to spawn a grandchild, and the cases it would have measured **fail with that reason** instead — the same number of cases in both worlds, and a loud red where there was an unbounded wait.

## No floor lowered, no case removed

`SELF_TEST_BATTERIES` floors are untouched; the roster's own size floor moves 22 → 23 with the battery added to it. No case is deleted or skipped, no other script is touched, and the post-merge audit's verdicts are unchanged — `--test` on this file still answers NOT governed at exit 0.

## Verification (union re-run at `d510d4ec`, after the final commit)

Repro, exit codes captured by redirect, never through a pipe:

| | before install | after install |
|:--|:--|:--|
| on `origin/main` | **exit 1** — "below its pinned floor of 7" | exit 0 — 245 assertions |
| on this branch | **exit 3** — PREREQUISITE NOT MET, prerequisite and remedy named | exit 0 — 262 assertions |

- **24/24 derived gates green**, re-derived for the actual changed path with `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (identical to the dispatched list; no family added).
- 7 artifact rosters whose list lives under `scripts/` also run: 6 green. `check:published-readme-exports` reports 1, entirely on unbuilt `dist/` entries in packages this diff does not touch (its own `--self-test` passes; filed separately as a finding of the same class as this card).
- Whole-repo `pnpm lint` green through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (VERDICT command-exit 0, held 75s, waited 0s) — the full scan, not a narrowing.
- `bash .claude/hooks/guard-governed-enqueue.selftest.sh`: 49 passed, 0 failed (the hook imports this file's `--test`).
- Ablation (a): probe removed → the uninstalled checkout reports `registered 5 case(s), below its pinned floor of 7` again, exit 1 — the card's exact shape.
- Ablation (b): probe in place, one case genuinely deleted → exit 1 naming `"the governed predicate: the 2026-08-18 unified list, exactly" registered 7 case(s), below its pinned floor of 8`. The floor still bites.
- Both ablations ran from the committed state with restore traps on absolute paths; each restore proven by `git hash-object` equal to the HEAD blob with an empty `git diff HEAD` and an empty `git status --porcelain`.

Tooling-only (`scripts/pm/**`), publishes nothing ⇒ `skip-changeset`.
